tools.description: Tween through a set of points on a curve, if points are not on the curve they will be pulled to it.

inputs.description: Set of points on curve to tween through
inputs.name: Points

inputs.description: Curve to tween point on
inputs.name: Curve

inputs.description:
Tween factor (0.0 = Point at index 0, Index number of last point = Point at last index), unless Normalized is true

The tween factor range from one point to the next point in the list is:
Index number of a point = the point at that index, Index number of the next point = the next point in the list, factors between the point index numbers will be the corresponding tweens.

For instance:
A tween factor of 2.5 will result in a tween point halfway between the point at index 2 and the point at index 3.
inputs.name: Factor

inputs.description: If True, use a normalized tween factor (Factor 0.0 = Point at P start, Factor 1.0 = Point at P end)
inputs.name: Normalized

inputs.description:
If False, the rules for factor are (0.0 = Plane at index 0, Index number of last plane = Plane at last index)

The tween factor range from one plane to the next plane in the list is:
Index number of a plane = the plane at that index, Index number of the next plane = the next plane in the list, factors between the plane index numbers will be the corresponding tweens.

For instance:
A tween factor of 2.5 will result in a tween plane halfway between the plane at index 2 and the plane at index 3.

tools.name: Twisted Box Consecutive Surfaces
tools.description: Create a layered array of connected twisted boxes consecutively between a set of surfaces from domain dividing parameters.

inputs.description: Set of surfaces to create twisted box array between
inputs.name: Surfaces

inputs.description:
Division parameters along surface {u} domains ({u}0.0 = Surface starts, {u}1.0 = Surface ends)

For best results {u} parameters should be between 0 and 1, in numerical order, and non duplicate
inputs.name: Parameters U

inputs.description:
Division parameters along surface {v} domains ({v}0.0 = Surface starts, {v}1.0 = Surface ends)

For best results {v} parameters should be between 0 and 1, in numerical order, and non duplicate
inputs.name: Parameters V

inputs.description:
Division parameters between each surfaces {w} domain ({w}0.0 = Surface at S, {w}1.0 = Surface at S +1)

For best results {w} parameters should be between 0 and 1, in numerical order, and non duplicate
inputs.name: Parameters W

inputs.description: If True, parameters {w} distribution is weighted by the input surface set and the interpolation path curvature
inputs.name: Weighted

inputs.description: If True, allow the parameters {w} interpolation path to continue from the end back to the start as a closed loop
inputs.name: Loopback

inputs.description: Curvature degree of the {w} interpolation path, degree should be a positive odd number
inputs.name: Degree

inputs.description:
Determines how the {w} interpolation path is interpolated

0 = Linear
1 = Chord
2 = Square Root
3 = Uniform
inputs.name: Interpolation Type

inputs.description:
Optional Refit match method.
(No Integer or 0 = Off, Integer greater than 0 = On and surface degree of refit)

If an integer greater than zero, Refit match method is used if possible. When input surfaces are refit their control points are redistributed, added to, and removed from based on the surfaces curvature and the input integer degree, while trying to maintain their shapes. Refit results in tighter shaped twisted boxes, with curvature based control point distribution.
inputs.name: Refit

inputs.description:
Optional Point Sample match method.
(No Integer or 0 = Off, Integer greater than 0 = On and amount of sample points) 

If an integer greater than zero, Point Sample match method is used. When input surfaces are sampled their control points are recreated by equally dividing the surface by the input integer point count. Point Sample results in looser shaped twisted boxes, with uniform control point distribution.
inputs.name: Point Sample

0 = Linear

inputs.description:
Optional Refit match method.
(No Integer or 0 = Off, Integer greater than 0 = On and surface degree of refit)

If an integer greater than zero, Refit match method is used if possible. When input surfaces are refit their control points are redistributed, added to, and removed from based on the surfaces curvature and the input integer degree, while trying to maintain their shapes. Refit results in tighter shaped tweens, with curvature based control point distribution.
inputs.name: Refit

inputs.description:
Optional Point Sample match method.
(No Integer or 0 = Off, Integer greater than 0 = On and amount of sample points) 

If an integer greater than zero, Point Sample match method is used. When input surfaces are sampled their control points are recreated by equally dividing the surface by the input integer point count. Point Sample results in looser shaped tweens, with uniform control point distribution.
inputs.name: Point Sample

constructor: Blend consecutively between a set of meshes by their vertices with a set of blend factors where each factor controls the blend amount between each set of vertices which share the same vertex index from mesh to mesh, meshes must have the same topology. Can also blend mesh vertex colors.
tools.name: Blend Consecutive Meshes
tools.description: Blend consecutively between a set of meshes by their vertices with a set of blend factors where each factor controls the blend amount between each set of vertices which share the same vertex index from mesh to mesh, meshes must have the same topology. Can also blend mesh vertex colors.

inputs.description: Set of meshes to blend between
inputs.name: Meshes

inputs.description:
Blend factors, one factor for each set of vertices which share the same vertex index from mesh to mesh
(0.0 = Mesh at M vertices, 1.0 = Mesh at M +1 vertices)
inputs.name: Factors

inputs.description: If True, blend distribution is weighted by the input mesh sets vertices and the vertex blend paths curvatures
inputs.name: Weighted

inputs.description: If True, allow the blend path to continue from the end back to the start as a closed loop
inputs.name: Loopback

inputs.description: Curvature degree of the vertex blend paths, degree should be a positive odd number
inputs.name: Degree

inputs.description:
Determines how the vertex blend paths are interpolated

0 = Linear
1 = Chord
2 = Square Root
3 = Uniform
inputs.name: Interpolation Type

inputs.description:
Determines how mesh vertex colors are blended

0 = None
1 = Fast
2 = Accurate
inputs.name: Colored Type

constructor: Blend through a set of meshes by their vertices with a set of blend factors where each factor controls the blend amount through each set of vertices which share the same vertex index across the meshes, meshes must have the same topology. Can also blend mesh vertex colors.
tools.name: Blend Through Meshes
tools.description: Blend through a set of meshes by their vertices with a set of blend factors where each factor controls the blend amount through each set of vertices which share the same vertex index across the meshes, meshes must have the same topology. Can also blend mesh vertex colors.

inputs.description: Set of meshes to blend through
inputs.name: Meshes

inputs.description:
Blend factors, one factor for each set of vertices which share the same vertex index across the meshes
(0.0 = Mesh at M start vertices, 1.0 = Mesh at M end vertices), unless Normalized is False
inputs.name: Factors

inputs.description:
If False, the rules for factor are (0.0 = Mesh at index 0 vertices, Index number of last mesh = Mesh at last index vertices)

The blend factor range from one mesh's vertices to the next mesh's vertices in the list is:
Index number of a mesh = the vertices of the mesh at that index, Index number of the next mesh = the vertices of the next mesh in the list, factors between the mesh index numbers will be the corresponding mesh vertex blends.

For instance:
A blend factor of 2.5 will result in blend mesh vertices halfway between the mesh at index 2's vertices and a mesh at index 3's vertices.
inputs.name: Normalized

inputs.description: If True, blend distribution is evaluated along the vertex blend paths without considering the locations of the input mesh sets vertices
inputs.name: Equalized

inputs.description: If True, blend distribution is weighted by the input mesh sets vertices and the vertex blend paths curvatures
inputs.name: Weighted

inputs.description:
If True, allow the blend path to continue from the end back to the start as a closed loop
(if Normalized is False, increase the blend factor range maximum by 1)
inputs.name: Loopback

inputs.description: Curvature degree of the vertex blend paths, degree should be a positive odd number
inputs.name: Degree

inputs.description:
Determines how the vertex blend paths are interpolated

0 = Linear
1 = Chord
2 = Square Root
3 = Uniform
inputs.name: Interpolation Type

inputs.description:
Determines how mesh vertex colors are blended

0 = None
1 = Fast
2 = Accurate
inputs.name: Colored Type

If an integer greater than zero, Refit match method is used if possible. When input curves are refit their control points are redistributed, added to, and removed from based on the curves curvature and the input integer degree, while trying to maintain their shapes. Refit results in tighter shaped averages, with curvature based control point distribution.

(No Integer or 0 = Off, Integer greater than 0 = On and amount of sample points)

tools.name: Average Curve
tools.description: Solve the arithmetic average for a set of curves.

inputs.description: Set of curves for averaging
inputs.name: Curves

inputs.description:
Optional Refit match method.
(No Integer or 0 = Off, Integer greater than 0 = On and curve degree of refit)

If an integer greater than zero, Refit match method is used if possible. When input curves are refit their control points are redistributed, added to, and removed from based on the curves curvature and the input integer degree, while trying to maintain their shapes. Refit results in tighter shaped averages, with curvature based control point distribution.
inputs.name: Refit

inputs.description:
Optional Point Sample match method.
(No Integer or 0 = Off, Integer greater than 0 = On and amount of sample points) 

If an integer greater than zero, Point Sample match method is used. When input curves are sampled their control points are recreated by equally dividing the curve by the input integer point count. Point Sample results in looser shaped averages, with uniform control point distribution.
inputs.name: Point Sample

The tween factor range from one curve to the next curve in the list is:
Index number of a curve = the curve at that index, Index number of the next curve = the next curve in the list, factors between the curve index numbers will be the corresponding tweens.

ports.name: Factor

ports.description: 0 = Linear1 = Chord2 = Square Root3 = Uniform
ports.name: Interpolation Type

ports.description: Optional Refit match method.(False = Off, True = On)If true, Refit match method is used if possible. When input surfaces are refit their control points are redistributed, added to, and removed from based on the surfaces curvature without changing their shapes. Refit results in tighter shaped tweens, with curvature based control point distribution.
ports.name: Refit

ports.description: Optional Sample Point match method.(No Integer or 0 = Off, Integer greater than 0 = On and amount of sample points per direction) If an integer greater than zero, Sample Point match method is used. When input surfaces are sampled their control points are recreated by equally dividing each direction by the input integer. Sample point results in looser shaped tweens, with uniform control point distribution.
